title: Chapter 96
content:
The clear afternoon sky was beginning to bruise with gathering storm clouds as they made their way down the steep slope.

Outside the little sundry shop, the elderly grandmother was still perched on the wooden deck, methodically peeling cloves of garlic. Jakyeong turned to Il-hyun and asked to borrow his wallet. Pulling out several crisp, high-denomination bank drafts, he stepped over and pressed the paper into the old woman's calloused palms.

Her heavy, sagging eyelids lifted in mild surprise as she peered up at him.

Jakyeong lifted a mesh sack of peeled garlic from the deck, giving it a playful shake. "For the garlic, ma'am."

Her cloudy eyes darted between the exorbitant bank checks and the young man's face, struggling to read the denominations. Jakyeong offered a soft smile, turning on his heel toward the car.

Before he could reach the door, a high-pitched shout cracked through the alley.

The grandmother shuffled over as fast as her bowed legs would carry her, thrusting the cash back into his hands along with two cold glass bottles of juice.

"You're the little boy from the house up top, aren't you?"

Jakyeong froze, the breath trapped in his throat.

Plucking the sack of garlic straight from his grip, a gentle, weathered smile carved deep into the woman's wrinkled face.

"What're you taking this for? You don't even know how to cook it."

"..."

"Still got those bright, sharp eyes. Not a bit of you changed since you were small."

She clicked her tongue with a fond, raspy chuckle and shuffled back toward the shop, her frail, hunched spine looking heartbreakingly small.

Jakyeong stared down at the glass bottles in his palms.

She remembered.

After all these years... someone actually remembered me.

A thick, hot lump rose in his throat. Watching the old woman's retreating back, he sprinted forward, shoved the thick wad of bank drafts deep into the pocket of her faded apron, and bolted back to the car before she could protest.

"For the bread," he whispered.

He threw the roadster into gear, descending the winding concrete lanes as fat raindrops began spattering against the glass. In the rearview mirror, the frail silhouette of the grandmother remained standing by the curb, watching until the car rounded the bend.

"What's on your mind?"

Jakyeong pulled his eyes from the mirror, looking across at Il-hyun. "It feels strange."

"How so?"

"I spent years thinking coming back here would be agonizing... but it wasn't bad at all."

"I'm glad."

The restraint was unexpected. Jakyeong had fully braced himself for the man to milk the moment for endless bragging rights, but Il-hyun simply offered that quiet, contented murmur.

"Thank you..."

The gratitude slipped past Jakyeong's lips after a long, hesitant beat. If Il-hyun hadn't dragged him here, he never would have found the courage to face those ghosts.

Thankfully, the sudden shower was brief; by the time they reached the downtown district, the clouds had parted into a brilliant, washed sky.

They stopped at a trendy boutique café to grab a drink. Packed with patrons seeking shelter from the earlier rain, the interior was lively and warm. After ordering at the counter, they found a small table by the panoramic window.

When the buzzer chimed, Jakyeong moved to stand, but Il-hyun caught his wrist, rising to fetch the order himself.

Watching the towering, impeccably tailored CEO carry a small wooden tray across the crowded café was a remarkably surreal sight. He moved with effortless, steady poise, completely unbothered by the trail of curious, admiring glances tracking his every step.

Il-hyun set the tray down, sliding a tall glass of fresh watermelon juice across the wood.

"Drink up."

Il-hyun lifted his own double espresso, taking a tiny sip before his brow pinched into a sharp, bitter scowl.

"How is it?" Jakyeong asked.

Il-hyun’s eyes turned dangerously cold. "If this barista were on my payroll, I'd have fired him on the spot."

Jakyeong let out a muffled snort, taking a long pull of his juice. It was leagues below the fresh purées the senior housekeeper whipped up at the estate, but refreshing enough.

"You really have a weakness for watermelon, don't you?"

"It's good."

"Want to pack it all in and buy a farm out in the countryside? We can grow watermelons together."

Jakyeong studied the man's unreadable expression, entirely unsure whether to take the bait. "Will you pay me a salary?"

"We're practically engaged, darling. What's mine is yours."

Jakyeong choked, nearly spraying crushed ice across the glass tabletop. He frantically scanned the room to see if anyone had overheard.

Engaged? Since when?!

He glared daggers across the table, but Il-hyun casually unlocked his phone, proudly displaying the chaotic selfie from the hillside cottage as legal evidence.

Jakyeong aggressively bit down on his straw. "You just do whatever you want, don't you? First making up wild lies about ancient burial rites this morning, and now this."

"Who said I was lying?"

Jakyeong scoffed. "You expect me to believe you actually intend to drag me into your grave? Stop trying to scare me."

Without a word, Il-hyun dialed a contact and tapped the speakerphone icon.

The line rang twice before a polished, professional voice answered:

"Park here, President Kang."

[Ah, Attorney Park. To what do I owe the direct call? Did a legal complication arise?]

"Regarding the personal clause we discussed last week. Has the draft been finalized?"

A strained, deeply uncomfortable pause stretched across the speaker. Finding it hard to hear over the café chatter, Jakyeong leaned his entire upper body across the table, pressing his ear closer to the device.

[Regarding that... from both a statutory and fundamental human rights perspective, the request presents severe ethical liabilities—]

"Counselor."

[Yes, President Kang.]

"If I had any interest in legal boundaries or moral ethics, why on earth would I retain your firm at seven figures a year? Am I mistaken?"

[No, sir... You are entirely correct.]

"Splendid. How difficult can it possibly be to secure a burial plot for two?"

Though speaking into the phone, Il-hyun’s dark, smoldering gaze remained pinned dead onto Jakyeong’s face, smiling with terrifying affection.

Jakyeong silently mouthed a vicious string of obscenities around his straw.

He wasn't bluffing. This lunatic genuinely updated his last will and testament to have me buried alive.

Ending the call, Il-hyun propped his chin on his knuckles, beaming like a proud schoolboy. "You heard the counselor."

"I'm choosing to suffer from temporary hearing loss."

"Accept your destiny, darling."

"Getting entombed alive with a psychopath is not part of my five-year plan."

Seeing Jakyeong’s devastated scowl only seemed to fuel Il-hyun's sadistic delight. Needing to escape the conversation, Jakyeong looked out the window, his eyes catching the marquee of a boutique cinema across the boulevard.

Il-hyun followed his gaze. "Want to catch a film?"

Jakyeong nodded without hesitation. A matinee screening followed by an early dinner sounded like an ideal trajectory. To ordinary couples, it was the baseline definition of mundane; to two men who spent their lives bathed in gunpowder and blood, the normalcy was intoxicatingly rare.

Because it was a weekday afternoon, the indie theater was relatively sparse. Armed with a large tub of buttered popcorn and a fountain soda, they made their way into the dimly lit screening room.

Settling into the plush velvet seats, Jakyeong rested his drink in the cup holder.

While the pre-show commercials played, he casually scanned the room. Strangely enough, nearly half the scattered audience consisted of lone men. Upon closer inspection, they sat with unnatural, rigid discipline—broad-shouldered figures staring straight ahead like carved stone.

The sight nagged at his instincts, pulling his eyes back every few seconds.

The theater darkened, and the title card faded in. It was a French arthouse drama detailing the bitter, agonizing unraveling of a long-term romance.

On screen, a woman was screaming hysterically at her partner, gesticulating with wild despair, while the exhausted man merely leaned back into his armchair, utterly detached. Left in isolation, the woman lit a cigarette, staring out a rainy window with a bottle of wine in hand.

The heavy, suffocating melancholy draped over the theater like a wet blanket. Forgetting the popcorn entirely, Jakyeong sneaked a nervous sideways glance at Il-hyun.

This is definitely not his genre. Why did I pick this?

Feeling the stare, Il-hyun turned his head. "Something wrong?"

Jakyeong leaned in close, whispering into his ear, "Is it boring?"

"Terribly."

Figures.

"Though I suspect things are about to get remarkably entertaining," Il-hyun added, a subtle, razor-thin smirk curving his lips.

He turned his focus back to the screen, leaving Jakyeong mildly relieved.

A moment later, a large hand drifted away from the armrest, gliding smoothly into the popcorn tub—only to bypass the snacks entirely, sliding down to rest firmly over Jakyeong’s inner thigh.

Jakyeong scowled, turning to swat the hand away, but Il-hyun silently mouthed two words: Right now.

Jakyeong caught the cue and bristled in disgust, trying to pry the fingers off. Slipping through his grip like an eel, Il-hyun’s palm boldly closed around his crotch, giving his shaft a firm, deliberate squeeze.

"Hey! Cut it out!"

The startled shout broke the quiet theater, drawing every pair of eyes in the auditorium straight to their row.

His face burning a furious, violent crimson, Jakyeong bit his lip and snapped his gaze forward—only to lock eyes with two men seated three rows ahead.

The pair averted their gaze with unnatural, lightning-fast precision.

The familiar, cold prickle of an ambush flared behind his ribs.

Setting the popcorn on the floor, Jakyeong lightly tapped the heel of his shoe against Il-hyun's shin.

Their eyes met. Il-hyun gave a microscopic tilt of his chin.

Moving in silent synchronization, both men stood and slipped through the emergency exit.

They darted into the elevator vestibule, hammering the ground-floor button. Just as the brushed-metal doors began to slide together, the heavy fire doors of the auditorium swung open, and three figures spilled into the corridor.

Ding.

The elevator sealed shut.

"You clocked them?" Il-hyun asked smoothly.

Jakyeong gave a curt nod. "The lone men in the theater. Dressed like civilians, but moving like contracted hounds."

"How did you spot them?"

"I recognized one of the faces from an overseas dossier."

"Is that why you grabbed my dick back there?"

"Not at all," Il-hyun replied with a disarming, boyish grin. "I grabbed it purely because I wanted to feel you up."

Of course you did. Jakyeong rolled his eyes.

The elevator reached the subterranean parking garage, the doors parting onto rows of parked luxury vehicles.

As they stepped onto the concrete, car doors clicked open across the bays in rapid succession. Half a dozen men in dark, tactical jackets emerged, cutting off the driving lanes.

Jakyeong and Il-hyun stopped in their tracks, conducting a rapid sweep of the garage. The exits were entirely sealed—a textbook perimeter containment.

There was no negotiation on the table; they had to punch through by force.

As Jakyeong shifted his weight to sprint forward, Il-hyun held out the key fob to the roadster.

Jakyeong caught it reflexively, blinking as Il-hyun delivered an absurd proposition:

"A wager, darling. Whoever reaches the driver's seat first wins."

Jakyeong stared in sheer, unvarnished disbelief. "Are you seriously trying to play games right now?"

"If I win... you're wearing floral lace lingerie to bed tonight."

Jakyeong ground his teeth at the lewd, infuriating smirk. Give this bastard an inch and he takes a light-year.

"And if I win? Do I get to drill you in the ass?"

"Be my guest, darling."

The sheer, arrogant confidence dripping from the man was enough to make Jakyeong's blood boil.

Flashing a wicked, predatory grin, Jakyeong reached behind his lower back, drawing a suppressed automatic pistol from the waistband of his slacks.

He slotted the magazine home and racked the slide with a crisp CLACK.

Kang Il-hyun’s smile vanished instantly, his jaw dropping in pure outrage.

"Where the hell did you hide a firearm?! That's a blatant technical foul!"

"If you feel wronged, President Kang... go find yourself a gun."

"You little—!"

Jakyeong rolled his neck, loosened his shoulders, and broke into an explosive sprint toward the front line.

"First one to the car wins! Keep your promise!"
